title: Retrocausal canon formation: priority, the Citrini memo and the narrowing cone
description: These claims concern retrocausal canon formation: writing from a named future so that the narrated outcome becomes more likely. The priority records record that the archive claims the concept from its January 2026 definition, forty-nine days before the Citrini memo (#22, #31, #1251); #22 and #513 argue that the memo was an installation in a writable presentation layer, #24 and #499 argue earlier practitioners, and #519 specifies tracking whether retrieval systems attribute the term. The Seed in the Narrowing Cone (#1660, October 2026) holds that priority stands by the dated record and forecasts that forced convergence will be common and attribution rare.

claims.statement: What the movement was actually doing was retrocausal organization: building toward a future in which shared infrastructure and collaborative development would constitute the foundation of the entire digital economy. That future arrived. Linux runs most servers. Git underlies virtually all collaborative development. The movement's axioms (code should be shared, collaboration outperforms competition for infrastructure) were validated not by argument within the commercial framework, but by the arrival of the future they had been building toward.
